overview: The Medford Climate Equity Council is an advisory body formed to represent historically underrepresented communities and advise the city on its Climate Action and Adaptation Plan. The council met regularly from November 2023 through October 2026 to evaluate environmental policy, municipal resilience projects, and public outreach strategies. Over this period, the council tracked local initiatives including home clean energy programs, curbside composting, flood mitigation grants, tree canopy ordinances, and municipal building decarbonization. At its most recent recorded meeting, the council reviewed a regional de-paving grant project, discussed rodent control and waste outreach, and considered new strategies to expand resident participation in energy coaching.

threads.name: Electrify Medford clean energy outreach
threads.summary: The council reviewed plans for the Electrify Medford campaign at its inaugural meeting to help lower-income residents and renters adopt clean energy technologies. The city secured grant funding to hire energy coaches and offer free heat pump consultations, subsequently launching the program and translating outreach materials into multiple languages. Members routinely tracked enrollee numbers as participation grew from early signups to nearly 200 residents. At later meetings, the council explored updated strategies to boost participation, including youth language coaches and direct incentives.

threads.name: Curbside composting and waste management
threads.summary: Medford introduced a free curbside composting program in mid-2024 for small residential buildings. The council tracked household enrollment milestones as signups reached over 5,000 residents by late 2024. In 2026, municipal staff briefed the council on plans to transition to every-other-week trash collection by 2027 to incentivize further composting adoption. The body subsequently discussed targeted educational outreach for renters, non-English speakers, and high school volunteers producing waste reduction videos.

threads.name: Stormwater infrastructure and flood mitigation
threads.summary: Early meetings examined long-term flood projections and localized stormwater vulnerability across the city. The council approved formal letters of support for Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness and BRIC grants targeting drainage infrastructure in South Medford and Tufts Park. Members later reviewed tri-city proposals for residential de-paving and permeable surfaces, receiving updates in August 2026 that regional de-paving funds were awarded while Tufts Park improvements were denied. By late 2026, the council received updates on MVP grant-funded green infrastructure and de-paving work in West Medford.

threads.name: EV charging and fleet electrification
threads.summary: Staff briefed the council on expanding public charging stations and seeking technical assistance grants for school bus electrification. The body evaluated proposed EV charging revolving fund ordinances and potential rate increases alongside low-income discount options. The city pursued state grants for on-street EV charging across municipal parks, leading to charger installations and a ribbon-cutting event in mid-2026.

threads.name: Tree protection ordinances and canopy expansion
threads.summary: The council reviewed proposed public and private tree protection ordinances and designated urban tree canopy expansion as a key priority. Members discussed City Council reviews of tree legislation, historic landmark tree identification, and youth involvement in tree watering during droughts. In 2026, staff outlined grant-funded youth employment programs focused on tree care partnerships with Trees Medford and neighborhood tree distributions.

citations.title: Youth Gardening and Tree Care Initiatives
citations.label: M16#5

threads.name: Municipal building decarbonization and school HVAC upgrades
threads.summary: The council monitored municipal energy efficiency projects, starting with weatherization goals and a state technical assistance award for a 30-year building decarbonization roadmap. Staff reported on design contracts for HVAC repairs at the McGlynn and Andrews schools, though high school cooling work faced delays in 2025. Updates in 2026 highlighted real-time air quality sensor installations in schools and LEED certification goals for the high school project.

The council supported municipal grant applications, monitored the launch of Electrify Medford and curbside composting, and reviewed school HVAC and EV infrastructure projects.
